clue.text: Provider of milk and chips 0 in a mess

parts.note: chips are fried potatoes, called fries in American usage

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the two little words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dairy farmer's lunch of chips has been spilt everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '0' is a printing mark. 'in a mess' supplies its own two words as fodder and signals their shuffle. A Friesian is a black-and-white dairy breed of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Friesian is a breed of cattle famous for its high milk yield.

clue.text: Mad female going to university with Chinese porcelain

parts.note: Ming is the dynasty whose porcelain vases are famous

explanation.surface: A woman heading off to college is furious about her heirloom vase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone furious is said to be seething or livid with anger.

clue.text: Virginia's batting on both sides — to no avail

indicators.note: the batting word stands on either side of the state's abbreviation, one copy each side

parts.note: a cricket side that is batting is 'in'
the same word used for the second side
VA is the postal abbreviation of the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A cricketer from Virginia keeps batting but achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is said to be 'in'; 'on both sides' asks for that word on either side of the state's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for effort that brings no result, uselessly.

clue.text: Draw attention to a modern complaint

definitions.meaning: nervous strain, often called an ailment of modern life

explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point is to put weight on it, and anxiety from pressure is the ailment of busy modern living.

clue.text: Secure island set-up for hermits

parts.note: to anchor something is to fix it firmly

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remote island colony is founded for religious recluses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' splits in two: 'up', in a down clue, turns the word 'set' bottom to top, after the island's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorites were religious recluses who lived walled up in a cell.

clue.text: Get cast adrift in boat

indicators.note: a boat cast adrift drifts aimlessly, so its letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to recover goods after being set loose in a dinghy.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to come into possession of it.

clue.text: Busy worker, disgruntled, is given reinforcement… (6,2) ..before or after busy worker has revolutionary fury

parts.note: the bee is proverbially busy and a worker bee is a type of bee
disgruntled means fed up

explanation.surface: An unhappy toiler is being propped up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strengthened has been bolstered or made sturdier.

clue.text: …before or after busy worker has revolutionary fury

indicators.note: has links the ant to the next piece placed beside it
after says the little word or comes behind the rest

parts.note: the ant is a proverbially industrious worker

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word for fury is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger or fury
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a hardworking insect was enraged earlier or later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the word for fury round; 'after' puts the literal 'or' at the end. The leading dots tie this clue to 6 for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior is the formal word for positioned at the front or earlier.

clue.text: Article about the holiday industry having no love for the practice of going unclothed

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the article is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: having no says the following item is removed

parts.note: the business of travel and holidays
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on the travel trade without romance turns to nudism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AN into NA; 'having no' removes O (love) from TOURISM, leaving TURISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudism is the practice of living without clothing.

clue.text: Michael's about to declare he's a rebel

indicators.note: about means around, so the name surrounds the verb

parts.note: Mick is a short form of the name Michael
to aver is to declare or assert

explanation.surface: Michael is on the point of announcing that he is a nonconformist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it is the container signal: the short name goes around the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an independent-minded nonconformist.

clue.text: Old airline gets bird to skedaddle

parts.note: BEA was British European Airways, a former UK airline
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A defunct carrier's mascot bird flies off.
explanation.walkthrough: BEA, British European Airways, merged into British Airways in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal imperative telling someone to go away quickly.

clue.text: Ink soon spreads over a fine cotton fabric

indicators.note: the rearranged letters lie over the letter A, enclosing it
ink that spreads runs and blurs, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spilt ink soon soaks across a delicate muslin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' signals the anagram of the first two words; 'over' wraps the result around the letter A, which sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nainsook is a soft, lightweight muslin originally from India.

clue.text: Are red letters more highly valued?

indicators.note: the clue asks for the letters themselves to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether red-letter days are cherished more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red letters' suggests red-letter days, but 'letters' signals the anagram of ARE RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prized above another is costlier or closer to the heart.

clue.text: Golfer, on crossing street, finds prime minister

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the golfer and the little word go around the street

parts.note: Arnold Palmer was a famous American golfer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer crossing the road spots the premier.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Palmerston was a 19th-century British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmerston served twice as Britain's head of government.

clue.text: Our musical arrangement is fantastic…

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorders the material, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A proud composer praises their own score as marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marvellous seems wondrous or beyond nature.

clue.text: One playing patience -initially each colour is turned up

parts.note: one is the article a

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the words it follows

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A card player at solitaire flips each suit's colour face-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes PP from 'playing patience'; EA abbreviates 'each'. Patience is the British name for solitaire.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive or show up is to make an appearance.

clue.text: Parmesan pie for old soldier

indicators.note: pie is printers' type jumbled together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheese pie is served to a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' (also spelt pi) is a printers' term for spilt, jumbled type.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearman was a foot soldier armed with a lance in older warfare.

clue.text: Consort of William IV face-up in a river

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a dial is a clock face

explanation.surface: A queen is found floating face-up in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face-up' splits: 'up' in a down clue reverses the word for a clock face, and 'in' puts that inside the river after A. The Dee is a river in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Adelaide was the wife of King William IV of Britain.

clue.text: … played with lots of flights of fancy

parts.note: piped means played on a pipe
reams means a great quantity

explanation.surface: Continuing 14: a marvellous piece performed with plenty of daydreams.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots link this clue to the previous one for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrealistic hopes are fantasies, like opium-pipe visions.

clue.text: Where one may find oneself after this type of job?

definitions.text: Where one may find oneself after this type of job?

parts.words: Where one may find oneself after this type of job?
parts.note: a robbery done with help from a staff member has the same name as the place a convict ends up: in prison

explanation.surface: A careers adviser asks where a certain kind of work leads.
explanation.walkthrough: An inside job is a crime committed with the help of someone in the organisation; afterwards the culprit may be in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for being in prison, which is where criminals end up.

clue.text: Refinement of language

explanation.definitionFit: Polish means sophistication, and with a capital it is the Slavic tongue of Poland.

clue.text: One working on newspaper may have prepared it — or a section of it

indicators.note: a section of says the letters form part of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A journalist may have written the piece or just one part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a section of it' signals the letters run within 'prepared it — or'.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who chooses and corrects copy for a paper.

clue.text: Make possible emperor's first detention centre on backward island

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter
centre takes the middle letter of the word
backward means read from right to left

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: An emperor's first prison camp sits on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes N, the middle letter of 'detention'; ELBA reversed gives ABLE. The surface evokes Napoleon's exile.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow or empower something to happen.

clue.text: Golf clubs in tree

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a wood is another type of golf club

explanation.surface: Golf clubs are stuck in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironwood is the name for various trees with very hard timber.

clue.text: Don't go for religious education to principal…

parts.note: RE is the school subject of religious education
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A head teacher is urged to stay for the RE class.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay behind rather than leave.

clue.text: …get theistic training with moral philosopher…

indicators.note: training shapes something into a new form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A believer's education produces a student of ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies right and wrong.

clue.text: …academic cardinal is an ass

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
cardinal means principal or chief, as does key

explanation.surface: A scholarly churchman is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman but means key, as in cardinal or key point.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a domestic beast of burden, the same animal.

clue.text: Release the 'orse outside

indicators.note: outside means the horse word goes around the article

parts.note: with the dropped H of Cockney speech, a horse for riding to hounds, a hunter, becomes 'unter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Cockney stable lad sets the horse loose outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''orse' marks a Cockney dropped H, so a hunter (a horse ridden to hounds) loses its H; 'outside' wraps it around 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something from a rope or tie.
